question: My dad had a bad accident and needs someone at home looking after him for a while. I had to stop working to do it. How soon should I apply for EI, and do I risk losing anything if I wait?
answer: Apply for EI as soon as possible after you stop working or after your earnings are reduced. If you wait too long, you may lose benefits. For other EI benefits, the documents say that applying more than 4 weeks after your last day of work may cause you to lose benefits, so do not wait that long. There may also be a waiting period depending on your situation. The documents say there is 1 week before you are paid, and if more than one caregiver shares benefits for the same person, only one of you serves that waiting period. The documents say that first payments usually arrive about 28 days after you apply, if you are eligible and have provided all the required information. You can save your online application and come back to it, but the information is kept for only 72 hours from when you started, so submit it within that time. Amounts and deadlines can change, so check the official page for the current rules. The page was last modified on 2026-06-02.

answer: The documents say the amount depends on your insurable earnings before taxes in the past 52 weeks or since the start of your last claim, whichever is shorter.
